overview.title: One route, at most one destination
overview.explanation: Flow arrows mean the next possible execution step, not ownership. Each successful handler returns to route immediately; there is no success arrow from the label desk to the general desk. The code blocks below show the early return that gives the overview this meaning.

focus.title: One handler can decline
focus.what: This function asks whether the label desk is responsible.
focus.where: route invokes it through the first Rule in the vector.
focus.why: A separate question can be reused without copying route.
focus.invariant: Declining must not create any printing side effect.
focus.risk: Returning a destination for every format prevents later rules from running.
explain: Define a handler that borrows a read-only job and returns an optional reply.
The comment explains that no reply is a deliberate decline.
Check whether the format is anything other than label.
Return the standard empty-optional marker when it is not a label.
Return a present string when the desk accepts the job.

focus.title: The stop rule lives in one loop
focus.what: This loop searches for the first present reply.
focus.where: It runs only after the page-count guard has accepted the job.
focus.why: The caller does not need to know the selected desk or the number of rules.
focus.invariant: Return at once on a present answer.
focus.risk: Replacing return with continued processing changes the contract into a different kind of chain.
explain: The comment states the first-handler policy.
Borrow each callable in vector order without changing it.
Call that rule with the same job and store its optional reply.
Check that a string is present before accessing it.
Return the string and end route immediately.
Close the loop after a decline, allowing the next rule.
Return an explicit unhandled result if no rule accepted.
